newsitem.title: USA: Texas crop maturity slowed by cooler temperatures.
newsitem.headline: Texas crop maturity slowed by cooler temperatures.

text.p: Cooler temperatures during the week ended Sunday helped slow crop maturity in the Texas Plains, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop upate.
Rainfall was not as heavy as it has been in previous weeks, although land preparation and harvest activities remained slow in many areas as wet fields kept producers idle.
Many open cotton bolls in central Texas have sustained damage from too much rain, and many dryland fields may have been "too far gone" to benefit from the rains, the report said.
Corn harvested 59 percent vs 63 year ago, 60 average.
Corn mature 75 percent vs 74 y/a, 70 avge.
Corn rated 75 pct good/excellent, 9 fair, 16 poor/v.poor.
Sorghum harvested 59 percent vs 67 y/a, 66 avge.
Sorghum mature 62 percent vs 78 y/a, 73 avge.
Sorghum rated 64 pct good/excellent, 28 fair, 8 poor/v.poor.
Cotton bolls opening 34 percent vs 33 y/a, 32 avge.
Cotton harvested 15 percent vs 18 y/a, 18 avge.
Cotton rated 42 pct good/excellent, 33 fair, 25 poor/v.poor.
Pasture and range condition was rated 29 pct good to excellent, versus 32 percent at that level last week.
